s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive respiratory symptoms with neck mass and laryngeal dysfunction
salient_findings: Progressive hoarseness and shortness of breath over 2 months
Fixed, oval-shaped mass on the left side of the neck
Displacement and immobility of the left hemilarynx with reduced respiratory space
key_facts: History of laryngeal tumour resection 14 years earlier
6-cm, fixed, oval-shaped mass on the left side of the neck
5.6-cm, hypodense mass with calcifications in the left subglottic laryngeal wall on CT
Infiltration and partial destruction of the cricoid and thyroid cartilages
No pathologic lymphadenopathy or distant metastases on chest x-ray or abdominal ultrasound

differentials: Adenoid cystic carcinoma of the larynx
per_call: Adenoid cystic carcinoma of the larynx

shortlist.label: Laryngeal chondrosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of laryngeal chondroma and current mass with calcifications

shortlist.label: Laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive hoarseness and shortness of breath with mass in the larynx

shortlist.label: Recurrence of laryngeal chondroma
shortlist.why_kept: History of previous laryngeal chondroma resection and current similar presentation

shortlist.label: Thyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass in the neck with infiltration of the thyroid cartilages

shortlist.label: Laryngeal adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive respiratory symptoms with a mass in the larynx

raw.rationale: The presence of a hypodense mass with calcifications in the left subglottic laryngeal wall, infiltration and partial destruction of the cricoid and thyroid cartilages, and significant subglottic luminal narrowing are consistent with a cartilaginous tumor such as chondrosarcoma, especially given the history of a previous laryngeal chondroma.

rejected.label: Laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: No history of smoking, intact mucosa, and absence of lymphadenopathy make this less likely

rejected.label: Recurrence of laryngeal chondroma
rejected.why: Chondromas are typically benign and the aggressive features such as infiltration and destruction of cartilages suggest a more malignant process

rejected.label: Thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: The mass is located in the subglottic laryngeal wall and involves the cricoid and thyroid cartilages, which is not typical for thyroid carcinoma

rejected.label: Laryngeal adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The presence of calcifications and cartilaginous involvement is not typical for adenocarcinoma
